newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Dacom shrs rise to upper limit.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Dacom shrs rise to upper limit.

text.p: Shares in South Korean telecommunications group Dacom Corp rose 7,500 won to their upper limit of 136,000 on Tuesday morning trading.
Brokers said the shares were boosted by rumours the National Assembly was considering a measure to allow individual shareholdings to exceed 10 percent in Dacom, considered a strategic business.

A speech by President Kim Young-sam on Monday underlining South Korea's plan to spend 10 trillion won by the year 2000 to support the information technology industry also boosted sentiment towards technology equipment shares, brokers said.

"It's just a rumour, but some players are saying that the National Assembly could pass a measure to allow major conglomerates to buy up to 33 percent stakes in Dacom from 1997. This is sparking mergers and acquisition talk again," said a Seoul Investment Trust Co fund manager who declined to be named.
Dacom could not be immediately reached for comment.
